key_insight: A proposed dense silicon spin-qubit architecture combines surface-code memories, shuttling lanes, and routing junctions to support scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing.
engineering_relevance: The design connects logical storage and gate operations with semiconductor-compatible integration and multiplexed control wiring.
method: Store rotated surface-code logical qubits in memories supporting logical single-qubit operations.
Connect memories through one-dimensional spin-shuttling lanes and cross junctions implementing transversal logical CNOT gates.
Evaluate logical errors using demonstrated device parameters and estimate capacity under multiplexed wiring constraints.
evidence_signal: The analysis estimates that code distance ≥21 is needed for logical errors below 10⁻¹⁰ per syndrome cycle and projects over 120,000 logical qubits on a 100 mm × 100 mm chip with optimized wiring efficiency.
watch_item: These are architecture-level estimates, not a demonstrated integrated system; scaling depends on reliable shuttling, junction operations, and optimized control wiring.
paper_title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
